greek: Τότε ᾖσεν Μωυσῆς καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ Ισραηλ τὴν ᾠδὴν ταύτην τῷ θεῷ καὶ εἶπαν λέγοντες ᾌσωμεν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐνδόξως γὰρ δεδόξασται· ἵππον καὶ ἀναβάτην ἔρριψεν εἰς θάλασσαν.
hint: Moses and Israel sing a song to God: the lord has thrown horse and rider into the sea.

notes.text: Let us sing to the lord: the Hebrew has ʾāšîrâ, I will sing, in the first person singular.

Gloriously he has been glorified, the adverb of ἔνδοξος beside the perfect passive of δοξάζω, for the Hebrew infinitive gāʾōh gāʾâ. Middle Liddell names the adverb, adv. -ως, and glosses it nowhere: see open question Q13.
δοξάζω, to think, imagine, suppose, Middle Liddell's first sense, and to magnify, extol its last; the perfect passive, and it stands so.

reading: [[at that time|at that time, then, in those times and formerly, at one time|τότε]] [[sang|sang, twanged, whistled, rang, sang and chanted, sang and praised|ᾄδω]] [[name:Μωυσῆς]] and the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[the song|the song and lay and ode, the song and singing|ᾠδή]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[to the God|to him who is God definitively, to the one the article marks out, to the known and the only|θεός]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling|λέγω]] [[let us sing|let us sing, let us twang, let us whistle, let us ring, let us sing and chant, let us sing and praise|ᾄδω]] [[to the lord|to the lord / master, to the head, to the master, to the Lord, to the Jehovah|κύριος]], [[held in esteem|held in esteem and honour and of high repute, notably|ἐνδόξως]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]], [[has been thought|has been thought and imagined and supposed and fancied and conjectured and it stands so, has been magnified and extolled and it stands so|δοξάζω]]; [[a horse|a horse and mare, horse and cavalry|ἵππος]] and [[one mounted|one mounted, a horseman and rider|ἀναβάτης]] [[threw|threw, cast, hurled, threw and tossed about, cast out, threw off and away, threw away and wasted, cast lots, threw and cast himself down, flung himself|ῥίπτω]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[sea|sea, the Mediterranean, a well of salt water|θάλασσα]].

(Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of Genesis 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")

greek: βοηθὸς καὶ σκεπαστὴς ἐγένετό μοι εἰς σωτηρίαν· οὗτός μου θεός, καὶ δοξάσω αὐτόν, θεὸς τοῦ πατρός μου, καὶ ὑψώσω αὐτόν.
hint: The lord has become helper and shelter and salvation; he is God, God of the father, and is to be exalted.

notes.text: Not in Middle Liddell: LSJ's shelterer, protector, citing this verse.
Helper and shelterer: the Hebrew has ʿozzî wĕzimrāt yāh, my strength and song is Yah.

reading: [[an assistant|an assistant, one assisting and auxiliary|βοηθός]] and [[shelterer|shelterer and protector|σκεπαστής]] [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence|γίνομαι]] to me [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[a saving|a saving and deliverance and preservation and safety, a safe return, a keeping safe, security and a guarantee for safety|σωτηρία]]; [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] of me [[God|everything that God is by nature, deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]], and [[I will think|I will think and imagine and suppose and fancy and conjecture, I will hold an opinion, I will magnify and extol|δοξάζω]] him, [[God|everything that God is by nature, deity in full and undiminished kind|θεός]] [[of the father|of the father, of the grandfather|πατήρ]] of me, and [[I will lift high|I will lift high and raise up, I will elevate and exalt|ὑψόω]] him.

greek: κύριος συντρίβων πολέμους, κύριος ὄνομα αὐτῷ.
hint: The lord crushes wars; lord is his name.

notes.text: The lord crushing wars: the Hebrew has YHWH ʾîš milḥāmâ, the LORD is a man of war.

reading: [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] [[rubbing together|rubbing together, shivering to atoms, beating to a jelly and crushing|συντρίβω]] [[battles|battles and fights and wars|πόλεμος]], [[lord|lord / master, the head, master, the Lord, Jehovah|κύριος]] [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] to him.

greek: ἅρματα Φαραω καὶ τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ ἔρριψεν εἰς θάλασσαν, ἐπιλέκτους ἀναβάτας τριστάτας κατεπόντισεν ἐν ἐρυθρᾷ θαλάσσῃ.
hint: Pharaoh's chariots and army are thrown into the sea; his picked riders and officers drowned in the Red Sea.

notes.text: καταποντίζω, to throw into the sea, drown therein, for the Hebrew ṭubbĕʿû, were sunk.
In the red sea, as at 10:19 and 13:18, for the Hebrew bĕyam-sûp; ἐρυθρός keeps the phrase's names, as at 10:19, and ἐν merges into its unit.

names.gloss: (Φαραω, from Hebrew Parʿōh, from the Egyptian for "great house")

greek: πόντῳ ἐκάλυψεν αὐτούς, κατέδυσαν εἰς βυθὸν ὡσεὶ λίθος.
hint: The sea covered them and they sank into the depths like a stone.

notes.text: πόντος, the sea, the open sea, in the dative, for the Hebrew tĕhōmōt, the deeps, the subject: the Greek has no subject but the lord.
The aorist of καταδύω, intransitive, to go down, sink, the causal senses left out.

greek: ἡ δεξιά σου, κύριε, δεδόξασται ἐν ἰσχύι· ἡ δεξιά σου χείρ, κύριε, ἔθραυσεν ἐχθρούς.
hint: The lord's right hand is glorified in strength and shatters enemies.

notes.text: Your right, the adjective with the article and no noun, and in the second line with χείρ beside it.
θραύω, to break in pieces, shatter, shiver, for the Hebrew tirʿaṣ, shatters.

hint: In great glory the lord crushed his opponents; his wrath consumed them like stubble.

notes.text: In the great number of your glory, for the Hebrew bĕrōb gĕʾônĕkā, in the greatness of your majesty.

greek: καὶ διὰ πνεύματος τοῦ θυμοῦ σου διέστη τὸ ὕδωρ· ἐπάγη ὡσεὶ τεῖχος τὰ ὕδατα, ἐπάγη τὰ κύματα ἐν μέσῳ τῆς θαλάσσης.
hint: At the blast of the lord's anger the water parted, stood like a wall, and the waves congealed in the sea.

notes.text: The water stood apart, the second aorist of διΐστημι: the Hebrew has neʿermû mayim, the waters were heaped up.

greek: εἶπεν ὁ ἐχθρός Διώξας καταλήμψομαι, μεριῶ σκῦλα, ἐμπλήσω ψυχήν μου, ἀνελῶ τῇ μαχαίρῃ μου, κυριεύσει ἡ χείρ μου.

greek: τότε ἔσπευσαν ἡγεμόνες Εδωμ, καὶ ἄρχοντες Μωαβιτῶν, ἔλαβεν αὐτοὺς τρόμος, ἐτάκησαν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες Χανααν.

greek: ἐπιπέσοι ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς φόβος καὶ τρόμος, μεγέθει βραχίονός σου ἀπολιθωθήτωσαν, ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ λαός σου, κύριε, ἕως ἂν παρέλθῃ ὁ λαός σου οὗτος, ὃν ἐκτήσω.
hint: May fear fall on them and the arm's greatness turn them to stone until the people the lord acquired passes by.
